title: Chilean Greenfield Mineral Projects — Development Pipeline
note: Compiled from public disclosures, company technical reports, government (Cochilco/SEIA) filings and industry press. Figures vary in vintage by project (noted per entry); some (e.g. Cerro Casale, NuevaUnión) have been stalled for years with no updated economics.

projects.name: Vizcachitas

location.detail: Putaendo district, ~150 km NE of Santiago, ~1,950 masl

projects.process_type: Open-pit mining, flotation concentrator, desalinated seawater supply

additional_data.notes: Considered one of the largest greenfield copper porphyry projects in Chile not owned by a major; faces environmental/community opposition.

projects.name: Cerro Casale
projects.owner: Barrick Mining Corporation / Newmont Corporation (50/50 JV; Newmont's stake inherited from 2019 Goldcorp merger)
projects.development_stage: Feasibility-level studies historically completed; no construction decision taken — long-stalled

location.detail: Maricunga gold belt, high Andean cordillera

additional_data.reserves_p_and_p_75pct_basis: 17.4 Moz Au, 4.3 billion lb contained Cu
additional_data.notes: One of the world's largest undeveloped Au-Cu deposits; reserve figures are from an older technical disclosure and have not been publicly updated recently. No confirmed construction timeline as of 2026. Project/JV also referred to as 'Norte Abierto'.

projects.name: NuevaUnión
projects.development_stage: Pre-feasibility level; long-stalled, no updated timeline
projects.process_type: Open-pit, planned use of desalinated seawater and dry-stack tailings

additional_data.notes: Combines the La Fortuna and Relincho deposits. Has not advanced to feasibility study in recent years; no current public NPV/capex figures.
One of only two mid-scale greenfield projects flagged by Cochilco as genuinely new (not brownfield) in its most recent portfolio report.
Second of the two greenfield projects specifically flagged by Cochilco in its current portfolio as genuinely new-build (vs. brownfield expansion).

projects.name: Proyecto Blanco (Salar Blanco)
projects.owner: Codelco (acquired via 2024 purchase of Lithium Power International / Minera Salar Blanco)
projects.development_stage: Environmentally approved (RCA granted); pre-construction, seeking a strategic/financial partner

location.detail: Salar de Maricunga, ~170 km NW of Copiapó, 1,125-2,563 ha of claims

projects.process_type: Evaporation ponds (traditional brine process); direct lithium extraction (DLE) also under evaluation

additional_data.notes: Would be Chile's third lithium operation after SQM and Albemarle in the Salar de Atacama, and the first outside that salar. Codelco is seeking a partner to help finance and operate it.

projects.name: Vicuña Complex — Chilean portion (Tamberías / Filo del Sol, Chile side)
projects.development_stage: Preliminary Economic Assessment (PEA, Feb 2026); integrated technical report filed Mar 2026

location.detail: Border zone with San Juan, Argentina; part of the binational Vicuña district

projects.process_type: Planned large-scale concentrator (Stage 1: 175,000 t/d, shared across the binational complex)

additional_data.notes: Formal binational operating protocol (PAE) under the Chile-Argentina Mining Integration Treaty approved August 2026. Tamberías deposit is wholly in Chile; Filo del Sol straddles the border.

projects.name: Los Helados
projects.owner: Nittetsu Mining / JX Advanced Metals (ownership in transition — Lundin Mining announced acquisition, expected to close April 2026)

location.detail: Near Lundin Mining's existing Caserones operation; part of the binational NexoAndino protocol (paired with Lunahuasi in Argentina)

projects.process_type: Not yet defined; potential synergy to process ore via Caserones' existing plant

additional_data.notes: Covered by the NexoAndino Additional Specific Protocol (PAE) approved under the Chile-Argentina Mining Integration Treaty in August 2026.

projects.name: Dominga
projects.owner: Andes Iron SpA (formerly Andes Iron) / project-level coordination with Chilean and international stakeholders
projects.process_type: Open-pit mining and concentrator; long-haul logistics and water-supply planning

additional_data.notes: One of the more prominent copper-gold greenfield candidates in Chile that remains in permitting and study stages rather than construction. Project economics and permitting timing have been subject to extended review.

projects.name: Pampa Camarones
projects.owner: Private Chilean project company / strategic investor group (project-level ownership varies by filing vintage)
projects.process_type: Not yet finalized; likely open-pit or bulk-tonnage mineralized system with conventional flotation

additional_data.notes: A notable northern Chile greenfield prospect that has not reached the same level of public maturity as the major porphyry projects listed above; status and capital estimates remain early-stage.

projects.name: Cerro Negro
projects.owner: Project-level ownership tracked via public disclosure; historically associated with Chilean junior mining interests
projects.process_type: Open-pit mining concept under evaluation; processing route not yet finalized

additional_data.notes: Representative of the broader early-stage greenfield pipeline in Chile's northern porphyry corridor; no final investment decision has been publicly announced.

projects.name: Llamara Lithium Project
projects.owner: Private project developer / strategic lithium investor group (ownership varies by disclosure period)
projects.process_type: Brine evaporation / lithium extraction concept under evaluation

additional_data.notes: Fits the category of greenfield lithium opportunities emerging outside the established Salar de Atacama basin; project economics and final process route remain in development.

projects.name: Salar de Pedernales Lithium Project
projects.owner: Private lithium developer / strategic project vehicle
projects.process_type: Brine extraction and evaporation-based lithium chemistry under evaluation

additional_data.notes: A representative greenfield lithium prospect within Chile's expanding salares pipeline; final engineering and water-use approvals remain unresolved.

projects.name: Pampa Blanca Copper-Gold Project
projects.owner: Junior mining company / project-level holding structure (ownership varies by filing period)
projects.process_type: Potential open-pit mining and conventional sulfide flotation

additional_data.notes: A district-scale copper-gold target in northern Chile that remains in the pre-feasibility-to-exploration phase rather than active construction.

projects.name: Cerro Chañar
projects.process_type: Open-pit orebody concept with conventional mineral processing under evaluation

additional_data.notes: An example of the broader northern and central Chile exploration pipeline, where project maturity remains early-stage and no fixed construction decision has been announced.

projects.name: Taltal Copper-Gold Prospect
projects.owner: Exploration-focused project owner / private mineral venture
projects.process_type: Bulk-tonnage mineralized system under exploration; process route not yet defined

additional_data.notes: Relevant to Chile's growing list of district-scale copper-gold prospects where greenfield status remains preserved pending a final feasibility decision.

projects.name: Mina de Oro de Maricunga

location.detail: Maricunga gold belt, high-altitude Chilean interior

projects.process_type: Heap-leach or conventional gold processing concept under review

additional_data.notes: The Maricunga belt continues to host multiple greenfield gold prospects; this entry represents one of the smaller but still relevant new-build candidates in the pipeline.

caveats: This is not an exhaustive list — Cochilco's 2025-2034 portfolio counts greenfield projects at only ~19% of a US$104.5 billion total investment pipeline, and many smaller-scale exploration-stage greenfield projects (e.g. those shown at industry events like FEXMIN) are not individually tracked here.
Cerro Casale and NuevaUnión in particular have far less current economic data available; both have been in a holding pattern for years without formal construction decisions.
Figures for capex, NPV and reserves come from different report vintages per project (ranging 2019-2026) — treat cross-project comparisons with caution.
